technical_and_design_decisions: Rename configuration mutators to SetXXX and implement replacement semantics for scalar, map, and keyed configuration values.
For slice-backed values such as anchor peers, implement idempotent replacement or insertion keyed by the relevant identity fields so duplicates are not created.
Rename ConfigTx.Base() and ConfigTx.Updated() to BaseConfig() and UpdatedConfig(), with deprecated forwarding methods retained only if they do not interfere with the intended API cleanup.
Introduce typed chained wrapper objects for the major configuration scopes, including channel, application, organization, orderer, and membership/MSP configuration.
Expose getters and setters through the chained wrappers while keeping protobuf conversion and validation centralized in the existing config transaction implementation.

Create an orderer subpackage containing orderer-specific types such as Kafka, EtcdRaft, BatchSize, and ConsensusState; leave shared policy behavior in the common package unless package ownership requires otherwise.
Create a membership subpackage containing SigningIdentityInfo, OUIdentifier, CryptoConfig, and NodeOUs, with the minimum necessary import and type-alias changes to preserve internal consistency.
Make removal operations idempotent: removing an absent value produces an unchanged updated configuration and no error.
Implement the sample CLI as a Go command in the repository, using subcommands and flags for genesis block generation, create-channel transactions, and configuration updates.
Use the existing protobuf/config transaction serialization and signing mechanisms rather than introducing a new wire format.
Use table-driven unit tests for replacement, removal, chained access, namespace migration, and CLI parsing/serialization behavior.
assumptions: The existing Hyperledger Fabric repository, build environment, protobuf definitions, and test infrastructure are available and functional.
The increment is implemented by one experienced Go developer familiar with Fabric configuration transactions and protobuf APIs.
The requested API renames may be breaking changes; deprecated forwarding aliases are added where practical, but complete backward compatibility for every old type name is not required.
The CLI is a functional sample/community tool rather than a production-grade replacement for configtxgen, and it does not require a new configuration-profile language.
The CLI must support all currently updatable configuration properties, but it may expose them through grouped subcommands rather than one flag for every property at the top level.
Cryptographic signing uses existing Fabric identities and utilities; no new certificate authority, wallet, or key-management subsystem is developed.
No changes are required to Fabric consensus algorithms, peer/orderer runtime behavior, network deployment, or generated protobuf schemas.
Documentation updates include package GoDoc, public API comments, command help text, README or usage documentation, and relevant code examples.
Existing tests and examples are updated as part of the refactor, and normal unit, integration, formatting, and static checks are included in the estimate.
The effort estimates include implementation, code review performed by the developer, test execution, and defect correction, but exclude elapsed waiting time and external stakeholder review.

activities.activity_description: Inventory the existing configtx types, Add/Update/Remove functions, ConfigTx lifecycle, examples, protobuf mappings, package dependencies, and CLI entry points. Define the wrapper hierarchy, naming strategy, namespace boundaries, and migration approach before coding.

activities.activity_name: Set mutator API and replacement semantics
activities.activity_description: Rename AddXXX and UpdateXXX mutators to SetXXX, implement overwrite behavior for scalar and map values, handle keyed replacement for slice-backed values such as anchor peers, update internal callers, and preserve validation appropriate to each value.

activities.activity_name: ConfigTx base and updated accessor rename
activities.activity_description: Rename Base() and Updated() to clearer accessors such as BaseConfig() and UpdatedConfig(), update all callers, and adjust associated API comments and compatibility forwarding methods where appropriate.

Implement typed intermediary objects for channel, application, organization, orderer, and membership scopes. Add chained getters and setters, connect wrappers to the underlying ConfigTx and ConfigGroup structures, and cover lookup, creation, and missing-scope behavior.

Create the orderer package and move or re-expose Kafka, EtcdRaft, BatchSize, ConsensusState, and related orderer-specific types. Update imports, constructors, type references, tests, examples, and package documentation without unnecessarily moving shared functions.
Create the membership package and move or re-expose SigningIdentityInfo, OUIdentifier, CryptoConfig, and NodeOUs. Update config conversion code, imports, tests, examples, and package-level GoDoc.

Update all removal operations so absent values are accepted without errors, return unchanged configuration when appropriate, revise error handling and signatures where safe, and document the no-op behavior in public comments.

activities.activity_name: Config API unit and regression tests
activities.activity_description: Add and update tests for Set replacement, duplicate prevention in slices, renamed accessors, chained retrieval and mutation, namespace types, idempotent removals, malformed inputs, and preservation of unrelated configuration data.

Improve New documentation, remove the specified trivial examples and Output validation, rename examples with valid GoDoc metadata, split broad examples into focused examples, update all calls to the new API, and reformat code blocks to avoid horizontal scrolling.

Build the Go CLI with command structure, flag parsing, input/output file handling, error reporting, genesis system-channel block generation, application create-channel transaction generation, and configuration update commands covering all supported updatable properties.

Add CLI unit and integration tests for command parsing, representative generation and update workflows, invalid arguments, serialization, and output files. Provide command help, usage examples, and sample invocations including anchor-peer updates.

Run and repair the complete Go test suite, example compilation, package documentation generation, formatting, lint/static checks, namespace import validation, and representative protobuf/config transaction interoperability checks.

Perform a final public API review against all acceptance criteria, inspect exported comments and compatibility impacts, clean up duplicate or obsolete code, verify release notes or migration guidance, and prepare the completed increment for submission.
